title: Why does my FFmpeg video look washed out?
fullTitle: FFmpeg -color_range pc Only Relabels: Black Shows as Gray 16

scenes.narration: Your encode looks washed out: black is gray. Is the video wrong, or only the label on it? We build a test card of pure black, pure white and two patches near the ends, encode it seven ways with libx264, and read the file.
captions: Black looks gray after an encode.
The pixels, or only the label?

scenes.narration: The card is lossless RGB: black zero, white two fifty five, patches at eight and two forty seven. Reader one is ffprobe for the range tag, plus signalstats. Reader two reads the raw luma byte. A player shows it as is if the tag says full, otherwise it stretches sixteen to two thirty five.

The default, dash pix fmt y u v four twenty p, writes black as luma sixteen and white as two thirty five, with no range tag. That is fine: players stretch sixteen to zero. Dash color range t v changes nothing. Same raw frame, still no tag.

Now dash color range p c. The raw frame is byte for byte the default: black still sixteen, white still two thirty five. Only the label changed, to full. A player that trusts it shows black as gray sixteen. That is washed out.
captions: Only the label changed: black shows 16.

scenes.narration: Real full range needs a conversion. Dash pix fmt y u v j four twenty p, or scale equals out range equals full, gives luma zero and two fifty five, tagged p c. Scale asked for y u v four twenty p and the file says y u v j. The control: full pixels with no label. Patches eight and two forty seven are crushed to zero and clipped to two fifty five.
captions: Control: no label, 8 and 247 are lost.

scenes.narration: Make the label match the pixels, and check with ffprobe and signalstats. Not tested: other ffmpeg builds, real players, real footage, other encoders, ten bit.
captions: Not tested: other builds, real players.
